rows.evidence: Q1: Section 'Deficit irrigation in fruit trees and vines', Fig. 10 and Table 1 <U+2013> the authors report their own long-term peach experiment near Cordoba comparing RDI, SDI and full irrigation (stem water potential, yield, fruit volume in the fourth year, 2005); acknowledgements mention technical assistance in the peach experiment.
rows.notes: The paper is predominantly a review of deficit irrigation, but it does include original data from the authors' peach experiment (RDI vs SDI at about two-thirds of control water: RDI kept yield and fruit size equal to full irrigation, SDI lost 10% yield), plus model fits of sunflower HI data. None of this concerns digital/app-based scheduling systems that combine crop stage, weather and soil moisture to decide when a deficit is acceptable; the scheduling in the peach trial was a fixed stage-based RDI regime monitored by stem water potential, not a digital decision system. The study therefore provides no own evidence on the technology named in the passage; it supports only the general deficit-irrigation principle (water productivity gains, stage sensitivity) cited in the neighbouring context.

notes: Full text appears complete. Mostly a synthesis/review paper with a small original-data component (peach RDI/SDI experiment, Fig. 10 and Table 1; Fig. 3 modelled alfalfa ET; Fig. 7-8 refits of Cordoba sunflower data).
